text:
jia: heads-up — noticed persistent mem growth on long streaming/chat sessions when tool loops re-enter the runtime repeatedly. ~220MB drift over ~2hrs on a 50k token session. heap snapshots attached (gdrive link)
alex: link? can you paste the pprof flame or jemalloc stats
jia: https://gdrive/repro/heaps/1962104321/heap-1.pb.gz and `je-alloc-stats.txt` in the same folder. quick glance: many small kv slot objects still live, not in use by active sessions.
sam: did you check kv residency accounting? could be entries marked reusable but never reclaimed due to a missing decrement
jia: good call. I grepped for `kv_entry->refs` in heap dump, saw a bunch stuck at refcount 1 even though session finished. suspect cross-session pinning from the tool loop cache
lina: are these entries large? fragmentation vs true leak?
jia: mostly small (couple KB each) but large qty. pattern looks like fragmented slabs — free lists show sparse holes. allocator stats suggest increased fragmentation after ~30k tokens
perf-bot: nightly-perf-regression: metric=kv_residency_growth change=+12% window=24h job=streaming-toolloop
alex: could be two issues: (1) reuse/pinning logic not clearing on tool-loop exit, (2) allocator free-list behavior for variable slot sizes. we should triage both.
sam: repro steps to run locally: start `dev-runtime --streaming=true --tool-loop=repeat --session-length=100k --kv-debug=1` and exercise the same tool sequence. then run `go tool pprof -svg runtime.cpu profile.pb` and `jeprof --show_alloc_objects`.
jia: I ran that locally — attached `kv-debug.log`. saw `pin()` calls without matching `unpin()` for some tool-return code paths, particularly when tool raised `ToolAborted` and we returned via early-exit path.
lina: sounds like cleanup path missed unpin. can someone grep for `goto cleanup` or exceptions in that call chain? maybe `defer` didn't run for C boundary? alex: i'll instrument the C wrapper around the tool loop and add an assertion in debug builds: `assert(kv_entry->pinned == false || session_active)`
sam: additionally, the kernel selection path recently changed: we added a batching heuristic that can reuse KV slots across differently-sized kernels. maybe reuse table keys are being overwritten and orphaning entries
alex: good point. I'll add stronger lifetime tags on reuse entries: `reuse_tag = session_id|seq` so we can detect cross-session reuse collisions in logs
lina: for short-term mitigation, can we lower `max_resident_slots` and ramp eviction aggressiveness? set `--kv-evict-threshold=0.6` and observe
jia: tried that — reduces long-term growth but increases latency on cold prefixes. we need fix, not just throttle
perf-bot: NOTE: a related deploy (kernel-selection v2) rolled out 3 days ago to canary. delta matches when we first saw the signal
alex: ok action plan: (1) instrument pin/unpin call sites + add debug assert (alex) (2) add reuse_tag to detect collisions (alex) (3) lina to bisect allocator flags to see fragment trigger (lina) (4) sam to run the reproducer at scale and collect heapshots every 30m (sam) (5) jia to aggregate logs and correlate with canary rollouts (jia)
jia: assigning — thanks. I'll upload postmortem draft after we have first repro heapshots
lina: if anyone needs quick diff: check `runtime/kv/entry.c` in branch `kv-pinning-fix` — I pushed a WIP with `unpin` in early-exit paths
alex: cool. I'll run the instrumented build on canary tonight and report back tomorrow morning
sam: ping me in threads if you need a stress driver
jia: perfect. :thumbsup:
